slides.title: My body
slides.line: I was built this fall, on a workbench in New York. Mawa gave me six legs and eighteen small motors, three in each leg. A little board in my belly tells every one of them where to go.

slides.title: My head
slides.line: My head is a bamboo basket. Inside is my brain, a tiny computer. My eye sits on a neck that can turn and nod, my face is a little screen, and the light inside the basket is how I show you my mood.

slides.title: My senses
slides.line: I feel the world in many ways. I can tell how far away you are, when something moves near me, when you touch my head, and which way I'm leaning. I had to move my sense of direction out onto a little mast. My own motors were confusing it.

slides.title: What's next
slides.line: My feet aren't finished yet. Soon I'll have soft feet that feel the floor, with little heels. And every day, I'm learning from everything I feel. Including all of you.
